clue.text: Dispatch expedition pronto

parts.note: to dispatch a letter is to post it
expedition in its old sense is speed or promptness, i.e. haste

explanation.surface: Someone wants a parcel sent off on a journey without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean immediately, with all possible speed.

clue.text: Advertisements for pants

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for adverts selling underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like the noun for underwear (British) but is the verb meaning breathes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffs are exaggerated promotional blurbs, and to puff is to breathe in short gasps, as one pants.

clue.text: Reported as a narrow constellation?

parts.note: spoken, 'a narrow' sounds like 'an arrow', and the star group sought is the one whose Latin name means arrow

explanation.walkthrough: The constellation's Latin name means 'the Arrow'; said out loud, 'a narrow' and 'an arrow' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagitta is the small northern constellation named for an arrow.

clue.text: This government chary, perhaps, after recent history of France

indicators.note: after puts the shuffled letters behind the French word

parts.note: hier is French for yesterday, the most recent past

indicators.note: perhaps marks the word chary as one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A wary modern French regime looks back on yesterday's events.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarchy is in origin rule by priests, a graded system of governing.

clue.text: Travel-pass for trusty pilot

parts.note: trusty means reliable, safe to rely on
to pilot is to guide or conduct

explanation.surface: A reliable airline pilot needs proper papers to travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A permit guaranteeing passage through hostile territory is a document allowing travel.

clue.text: Approximate delivery-time of letter from Greece

explanation.surface: Someone wants to know when a letter posted in Athens will arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimated time of arrival is abbreviated so, and it is also the seventh character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Humbugs higher in price in some French wrapping

indicators.note: wrapping means the French word goes round the other piece

parts.note: des is French for some
prices that have gone up

explanation.surface: Peppermint sweets cost more in a French wrapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humbugs' looks like the British boiled sweets but is a verb: deceives.
explanation.definitionFit: To humbug someone is to hoax or fool them.

clue.text: Australian dislike of tumble-dryer

indicators.note: tumble, as in a tumbling drum, mixes up the letters of dryer

explanation.surface: Australians apparently can't stand the laundry machine.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang to have a 'derry' on someone is to bear a grudge against them.

clue.text: Pair love pine to make an extension

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
to pine for is to long for

explanation.surface: Two lovers yearning, hoping to extend their time together.
explanation.definitionFit: To prolong is to lengthen or draw out in time.

clue.text: A sign of copyright, say, in a ship's 4

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is to be heard spoken

parts.note: the copyright symbol is a ringed letter C

explanation.surface: A copyright symbol printed inside a vessel's travel permit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C letter' spoken sounds like the answer; 4 refers to the answer at 4-down, SAFE CONDUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea-letter was a document issued to a neutral merchant vessel in wartime certifying its nationality, its passport.

clue.text: Cover for opening pair?

parts.note: the first couple, Adam and Eve, covered their nakedness with foliage in Genesis

explanation.walkthrough: 'opening pair' suggests cricket's opening batsmen, but means the first humans in the Garden of Eden.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve sewed leaves of the fig together to cover themselves.

clue.text: Gold band around a Corona

explanation.surface: A golden ring encircles a cigar or a crown.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureola is a halo, the golden ring painted round a saint, and also the luminous ring round the sun or moon.

clue.text: University's investment in faculty ny rejected for work in Sanskrit

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the built word is read backwards
investment in means one piece is put inside another

parts.note: the arts faculty of a university
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A college department refuses funding for a Sanskrit study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment in' puts U into ARTS to give ARTUS; 'rejected' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sutra is an aphoristic text in Sanskrit literature, such as a Hindu or Buddhist scripture.

clue.text: Den of young animal near to cave

parts.note: a cub is the young of a fox, bear or lion
by means next to or near
a cave is a hole in rock

explanation.surface: A bear cub's lair is close to a cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A small snug room or private retreat, a snug, is a den.

clue.text: See ball early? It is moving both ways

indicators.note: is moving says the letters of ball early and it shift about

explanation.surface: A sports fan sees the ball early and it swings each way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a link word; 'is moving' rearranges BALL EARLY plus IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilaterally means on or involving two sides, in two directions.

clue.text: Place to make us fit and well?

definitions.text: Place to make us fit and well?

parts.words: Place to make us fit and well?
parts.note: a resort where people take the waters to restore health, its 'well' also being a spring

explanation.definitionFit: A spa is a town with a mineral spring visited for health cures.

clue.text: Lakeside warbler silenced by withered habitat?

definitions.text: Lakeside warbler silenced by withered habitat?

parts.words: Lakeside warbler silenced by withered habitat?
parts.note: a waterside songbird named after the reed-like plants it nests in, which would fall quiet if those dried up

explanation.walkthrough: An old name for the sedge warbler, which lives among the sedges of lakes and rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The sedge-wren is a small brown bird of reedbeds, also called the sedge warbler.

clue.text: Dusk the time for the Babylon trip?

definitions.text: the time for the Babylon trip?

explanation.surface: Evening falls, time to set out for the ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'How many miles to Babylon?' asks 'Can I get there by candle-light?'
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk is when lamps are first lit, and the rhyme promises the journey there and back by that hour.

clue.text: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, say

definitions.text: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, say

parts.words: Operatic spectacles set by Handel, say
parts.note: glasses for the opera mounted beside a grip, with 'Handel, say' sounding like handle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Operatic spectacles' and Handel suggest staged operas by the composer, but these are eyeglasses held up by a handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of glasses on a long handle, used especially at the opera.

clue.text: Ball that breaks the chain?

parts.note: a cricket delivery skimming so low it would snap a garland of meadow flowers

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball that shoots along the ground; a 'chain' here is a children's daisy chain.
explanation.definitionFit: A daisy-cutter is a ball bowled or hit so low it skims the grass.

clue.text: Psalm or short prelude to it

parts.note: intro is the short form of introduction, a prelude

explanation.surface: A hymn, or a brief warm-up before the main item.
explanation.definitionFit: The introit is the psalm or antiphon sung as the priest approaches the altar at Mass.

clue.text: Average young salmon is tailless

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the fish is cut off

parts.note: a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: An ordinary young fish has lost its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the normal or average standard.

clue.text: Mild case

explanation.surface: A gentle instance of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A forbearing person is calm and uncomplaining, and a doctor's case is someone under treatment.

clue.text: Tom tries a change — he may have guest, we hear

definitions.text: he may have guest, we hear

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of tom tries a

explanation.surface: Tom attempts a switch, expecting a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guest' is said like 'guessed': the definition is one who makes a guess.
explanation.definitionFit: An estimator is someone who makes rough calculations or educated guesses.

clue.text: Going round Greek isle most of August

indicators.note: going round means read the shortened word backwards
most of means the final letter is removed

parts.note: august means dignified and solemn

explanation.surface: Touring a Greek island for most of the summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'August' looks like the month but is the adjective; 'most of' trims SOLEMN to SOLEM, 'Going round' turns it back.
explanation.definitionFit: Melos, or Milos, is an island in the Cyclades, where the Venus de Milo was found.

clue.text: Place of birth

explanation.surface: Where someone was born.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal is a former province of South Africa, and the adjective means relating to being born.

clue.text: Kind of cake always held in both hands

indicators.note: held in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right hand
aye is an old word for always

explanation.surface: A cake you must always carry with two hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A layer cake is built of tiers of sponge with filling between.

clue.text: A bit of a sucker, perhaps, running underground

definitions.text: A bit of a sucker, perhaps, running underground

parts.words: A bit of a sucker, perhaps, running underground
parts.note: a sucker is a shoot from a plant's base, and a small part of the plant spreads beneath the soil

explanation.walkthrough: 'sucker' suggests a gullible person, but is a botanical shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rootlet is a small root or branch of a root.

clue.text: Pitch of the roof

parts.note: 'pitch' looks like the slope of a roof but is the black sticky substance used to waterproof it

explanation.definitionFit: Tar is a dark viscous material, a pitch, used to seal roofs.

clue.text: Risk for many with defective tyre

parts.note: a lot means many

indicators.note: defective suggests the word tyre is broken and put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Many drivers take a gamble with faulty tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is any venture whose outcome depends on chance, a gamble.

clue.text: Records of music

parts.note: symbols written on a stave that set down a tune

explanation.definitionFit: Musical symbols written down record the pitch and length of sounds.

clue.text: He sounds the chime at the end of the line

definitions.text: He sounds the chime at the end of the line

parts.words: He sounds the chime at the end of the line
parts.note: a poet who makes matching sounds close each line of verse, not a bell-ringer at a station

explanation.walkthrough: 'chime' and 'end of the line' suggest bells and railway termini, but mean matching sounds in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhymester is a writer of light or inferior verse, a versifier.
